- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3% downward correction in subsequent periods.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in forecast 3–5 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric correction: +1% early, -1% late.
